 Football
 Soccer-Carrick drops United captain Fernandes to bench against Bournemouth
 By Lori Ewing 
 Sunday, 25 Oct 2026
 | 9:24 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Soccer Football - UEFA Champions League - Como v Manchester United - Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, Como, Italy - October 21, 2026 Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes looks dejected after being substituted REUTERS/Alessandro Garofalo 
 MANCHESTER, England, ⁠Oct 25 (Reuters) - Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has dropped captain ⁠Bruno Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's Premier League home ‌game against Bournemouth, but said the decision was based solely on football considerations.
 Fernandes questioned United's approach after Wednesday's 4-1 Champions League thrashing at Como, suggesting the side ​had allowed their opponents too much time ⁠and space by sitting back ⁠rather than pressing aggressively.
 Asked before kickoff whether Fernandes had been left ⁠out ‌for football reasons or other factors, Carrick told Sky Sports: "Pure football."
 "When you have options it's always a difficult decision. ⁠We have to make the right one for today ​and the team ‌to get that performance we want," he added.
 Defender Harry Maguire ⁠will wear ​the captain's armband instead.
 After Wednesday's shambolic loss, Fernandes told TNT Sports: "The coaching staff decided not to press man-to-man, but instead to sit back and ⁠look to win the ball; the problem, ​however, is that you give teams like that confidence when you allow them that space."
 The Portugal international added that teams under pressure sometimes needed ⁠to be "braver" and take risks by pressing higher up the pitch.
 Carrick had refused to rule out disciplinary action when asked about the comments at his pre-match press conference on Friday. The midfielder was ​named among the substitutes against Bournemouth.
 Since Carrick's first ⁠game in charge in January, Fernandes has registered more assists (14) and ​created more chances (96) than any player in ‌Europe's big five leagues.
 United began the day ​15th in the table with just one win from seven league matches.
 (Reporting by Lori Ewing; editing by Clare Fallon)
